claims.statement: NACP is a Go reverse proxy for the Nomad API that owns admission-time mutation, validation, and response adaptation, not scheduling or durable job storage; Nomad remains the upstream job-state owner.

The executable composition root is cmd/nacp, which assembles reusable components under pkg after package restructuring; root generate.go is a package nacp generation stub, and release builds explicitly target ./cmd/nacp.

Bootstrap uses defaults only when -config is omitted; an explicitly missing file fails, and configuration validation checks listener/upstream constraints, controller types and required blocks, duplicate names, and bundle SDK prerequisites before serving.
run handles SIGINT and SIGTERM, shuts down HTTP with a 30-second deadline, propagates shutdown errors, and defers OPA and enabled telemetry cleanup.

Admission applies only to PUT/POST requests on /v1/jobs, /v1/job/<id>, /v1/job/<id>/plan, and /v1/validate/job; other traffic is proxied without admission, and actionable request bodies are capped at 32 MiB.

Registration and planning stop on admission errors with the current HTTP 500 error rendering; validation-endpoint validator errors instead accompany a forwarded mutated job and are inserted into a successful Nomad validation response, while mutator errors still abort.

NACP injects warnings and validation errors only into successful upstream responses, preserving non-2xx Nomad bodies; adapters handle plain/gzip bodies and content lengths, with warnings formatted by the local MergeMultierrorWarnings and written into response Warnings fields.
JobHandler runs mutators in configuration order, feeding each returned job into the next; missing input jobs, mutator errors, and nil returned jobs fail the chain before validation.

Validators receive isolated JSON-deep-copied versions of the final mutated job and aggregate their errors, while sharing the same request context pointer; validator job writes cannot change other validators' jobs or the forwarded job.

JobHandler depends on JobMutator/JobValidator interfaces and types.Payload rather than concrete integrations, and configurable extensions additionally require config validation and executable factory wiring; warnings alone are distinct from rejecting errors.

The configured controller surface comprises opa_json_patch, opa_bundle_json_patch, and json_patch_webhook mutators plus opa, opa_bundle, webhook, and notation validators; the tested whole-job WebhookMutator is library-only and has no createMutator case.

Local OPA controllers read and prepare their Rego query at construction and retain it for controller/process lifetime, evaluating each request payload without rereading the file; an empty result set fails, but absent or wrong-typed patch/errors/warnings binding collections are treated as empty.

One optional OPA SDK is created before server construction and shared by both bundle controller factories; its config file drives SDK services/bundles, startup readiness has a 30-second deadline, readiness failure stops it, and cleanup uses a 10-second Stop context.

Bundle controllers use the embedded SDK Decision call with the request payload and configured opa_sdk_rule.path; the bundle validator requires an object result and rejects malformed message collections or non-string entries, while missing/null message fields are allowed.

All three configured patch mutators converge on jsonpatcher.PatchJob, which applies JSON Patch to the serialized Nomad job rather than the payload or HTTP envelope and decodes the result into api.Job.

Configured webhook controllers send the combined job/context JSON payload with the configured HTTP method and compatibility identity headers; webhook errors reject admission, including errors from JSON-Patch mutators.

remoteutil centralizes webhook URL validation, a shared instrumented transport with a 30-second client timeout, and response decoding that rejects non-2xx, malformed JSON, or bodies over 10 MiB; webhook callers close their response bodies.

Notation ImageVerifier bridges Notation verification and ORAS registry access; standalone NotationValidator checks Docker task image strings and returns the first verification failure as a warning, whereas optional local-Rego notation_verify_image returns a boolean for policy-controlled enforcement.

TLS and image trust are file-backed deployment inputs: bootstrap constructs TLS configurations from certificate/key/CA files and image verifiers from a loaded trust-policy document, filesystem X509 trust store, and file-backed registry credentials.

Jobs, warnings, validation errors, and identity data are request-scoped; resolve_token is ORed across controllers and triggers actionable-request token lookup whose failure aborts, while the policy-visible ACLTokenContext excludes SecretID and ExpirationTTL.

NACP builds its chain from startup configuration and installs the proxy as its HTTP handler; it has no separate NACP health, storage, or configuration-reload API or file-watcher loop, and SDK bundle management is not a general NACP reload mechanism.

LoggerFactory fans slog records to configured text/JSON outputs and optional otelslog, while SetupOTelSDK installs enabled process-global log, metric, and trace providers with OTLP HTTP exporters and TraceContext/Baggage propagation using standard exporter environment configuration.
Incoming proxy handling and outgoing Nomad/webhook transports are instrumented with otelhttp, and JobHandler emits admission/controller spans and per-controller warning/error and mutation counters.

Metric definitions are maintained under pkg/o11y and generated wrappers in pkg/o11y/metric.go point to templates/registry/go/metric.go.j2; root generate.go still references ./o11y rather than the current pkg/o11y location, so generation paths need inspection before use.
The root nacp binary, dist directory, __debug_bin files, and coverage .out files are local build/debug outputs rather than maintained runtime design sources, as reflected by .gitignore.

The engineering regression boundaries are separated: cmd/nacp tests cover proxy compatibility, routing, factories, bootstrap and TLS, controller_test.go covers mutation aggregation and validator isolation, and policy/webhook adapters and patching have focused package tests.
Bundle tests use testutil.SetupOpa with a mock HTTP bundle server, while executable SDK tests separately cover valid/invalid configuration, disabled setup, missing files, and readiness timeout.

Notation registry tests are gated by the integration build tag, but the untagged OTel TestOtlpSetup launches a collector container, so untagged tests are not universally Docker-free; cmd/nacp telemetry tests use in-memory exporters, and provider/environment setup affects process-global state.

OPA SDK/bundle support coexists with local Rego; the current bundle validator type is opa_bundle while opa_sdk and opa_sdk_rule remain configuration block names, so current factories and configuration—not branch migration experiments—define the supported naming and wiring.

The Unreleased changelog documents admission-hardening behavior changes for route bypasses, validating the wrong job, token-resolution fall-through, malformed bundle decisions, and unsafe response rewriting; current code implements the corresponding guards rather than these being merely historical branch proposals.

The maintained Nomad-removal rationale identifies licensing and dependency weight as drivers; current go.mod retains only nomad/api rather than the Nomad server module, the MPL-2.0 v1.6.3 warning formatter preserves compatibility and notices, and TLS test helpers replace Nomad internals with standard-library code; the reported 510-to-258 module reduction is historical.
